زَالِجٌ : see زَلُوجٌ. ―
-b2- Also An arrow that slips (يَتَزَلَّجُ or يَنْزَلِجُ [see 5]) from the bow; (S, K;) and so ↓ زَلُوجٌ [q. v.]: (K:) or an arrow that is shot by the archer, and falls short of the butt, striking violently upon a rock, and bounding up from it to the butt: but such is not reckoned مُقَرْطِس: (AHeyth, TA: [see also زَالِخٌ:]) and ↓ زَلْجٌ , as though an inf. n. used as an epithet, an arrow that falls upon the ground, and does not go straight to the animal at which it is shot. (TA.) ―
-b3- Also Escaping from difficulties, troubles, or distresses. (K.) ―
-b4- And Drinking vehemently (K) of anything. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
